previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was readmitted for worsening shortness of breath and 5-pound weight gain, indicating acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, transitioned to oral torsemide 20 mg daily, and underwent a right thoracentesis that removed 3.5 liters of transudative fluid, significantly improving his breathing. His hyponatremia and acute kidney injury resolved with diuresis. Warfarin was held temporarily due to bleeding risk, and metoprolol was increased to 150 mg daily for rate control. A multidisciplinary discussion concluded that valve intervention was not beneficial. He was discharged home with home health services, on strict fluid and sodium restrictions, with instructions to monitor daily weights and follow up for INR checks and symptom management.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Other dependence on machines, supplemental oxygen
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male hx severe diastolic CHF, severe AS, moderate 
AR, AF, moderate pulmonary HTN,s/p pleurx placement on ___ for 
end stage heart failure and symptomatic managment of pleural 
effusions admitted with community acquired pneumonia, atrial 
fibrillation with RVR, and acute exacerbation of diastolic heart 
failure.

patient is usually maintained on ___ 80mg IV lasix 
infusion in clinic which were missed for the past two weeks due

4. Admission weight was 132 labs ( per the son his dry weight is 
114-116) and discharge weight was 54.3kg. Torsemide was 
continued at 40mg BID. 

# Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventriular response- The 
patient was admitted with in afib with RVR with hearts in the 
140s -160s with activity, but was asymptomatic. His rates were 
likely difficulty to control in the setting of heart failure and 
infection.  The patient is supposed to on metoprolol 100mg XL at 
home, however the son reports his dad does not take it home 
because of his blood pressure. He was started on metoprolol 
tartate 25mg q6H and his pressures were able to tolerate this. 
He was transitoned to metorpolol 100 mg XL while in house and 
his pressures were stable. In addition he was digoxin loaded to 
get better rate control. HRs improved to 110s-120s 
(fibrillation) and he was discharged on Digoxin 0.0625 mg daily, 
and metoprolol 100 mg XL daily. His coumadin was managed per 
below.

#Coagulopathy- The patient was admitted with a supratherapeutic 
INR of 5.5 Per discussion with the PCP office it is unclear if 
the paient is compliant with his coumadin. Also likely he was 
supratherapeutic from recent antibiotics as an outpatient. 
Coumadin was held on admission until INR was < 2.5. He was 
restarted on 6 mg 3X/WEEK (___), 4mg 4x/WEEK 
(___). INR was therapeutic at discharge.

# chronic pleural effusion- The patient was has a pleurex 
cathether for recurrent pleural effusion secondary to advanced 
diastolic heart failure which is drained 2x week at home. He had 
3L drained while inpateint. Inital pleural fluid studies were 
consistent with a exudate effusion which is likely parpneumonic 
from his right middle lobe and right lower lobe pneumonia ( see 
below). Pleural fluid cultures were negative. Repeat CXR after 
his effusion was drained showed signficant improvement. At 
discharge drainage of his Pleurex cathether should continue 3x/ 
week, or if not tolerated 2x/week.

# Community acquired pneumonia: CXR with right RLL and middle 
lobe consolidation concerning for pneumonia. Given his mild 
leukocytosis on admission and cough, he was treated with 
levofloxacin 750mg Q48 (___). His leukocytosis had 
resolved by discharge. Sputum culture was consistent with 
respiratory flora.

# Acute kidney injury - The patient was admitted with a sCr of 
1.6 which was likely secondary to renal vascular conjection from 
his heart failure. His Cr improved with diuresis. At discharge 
Cr was 1.1, at baseline.
